data.name: Dilip
data.gender_notes: Dilip is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'dilip', meaning 'one who has a light in their eyes' or 'shining'. In Hindu mythology, Dilip is a name given to various gods, including Vishnu and Shiva. The name Dilip carries the meaning “Light, Shining” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dilip usually hope their child will grow to embody light, shining and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Dilip belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Light, Shining.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dilip total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Dilip signifies 'rising sun' in Sanskrit. It is a symbol of hope, new beginnings, and the promise of a bright future. The name evokes the feeling of a new day full of possibilities and opportunities, inspiring the bearer to rise above challenges and shine bright.

historical_references.reference: There is a king named Dilipasaka in the Gangadharasana inscription of the Satavahana dynasty, dated around 2nd century AD. This king is believed to have ruled the eastern parts of the Satavahana empire, possibly the regions of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

Another inscription from the 11th century CE at Kannauj, Uttar Pradesh, mentions a Brahmin named Dilip. This inscription is related to the construction of a Vishnu temple and suggests that Dilip was a significant donor and contributor to the temple.
